result.note: Tested the August 2026 sweep against the Shahzad Bhatti Network and the law used for the arrests (UAPA); skipped the profile of Bhatti and the investigators' allegations.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the August 2026 security operation against the Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN):
items: Forces detained 253 people across 14 states in a coordinated sweep on 12 August 2026.
The Ministry of Home Affairs said the operation was timed to pre-empt attacks around Republic Day.
Grenades seized in the operation bore Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, which the Ministry of Home Affairs cited as evidence of cross-border links.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the MHA said the sweep was timed to pre-empt attacks around the 15 August Independence Day holiday. The seizures also included IEDs, pistols and live cartridges, and the SBN now faces more than 80 FIRs.
questions.source: On August 12, forces detained 253 people across 14 states in a coordinated sweep against the Shahzad Bhatti Network (SBN).

questions.prompt: In August 2026, under which law were arrests made in the crackdown on the Shahzad Bhatti Network, a Pakistan-based terror network?
questions.explain: The arrests were made under the UAPA, under which charges against the accused are deemed prima facie true and bail is an exception. The Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad says the network recruits young people through online radicalisation.
questions.source: The arrests were made under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), where charges against the accused deem to be prima facie true, and bail is an exception.
